title: Pantry Tomato Rice Soup
description: A simple pantry soup made with canned tomatoes, broth, and rice.
substitutions: Skip the onion if you do not have one.
Add frozen spinach or peas near the end.

steps.text: Add tomatoes, broth, rice, and seasoning.

cookSteps.text: Heat {{oil}} oil or butter in a medium pot. Cook the onion for 3–4 minutes if using.
Add the crushed tomatoes, {{broth}} broth, {{rice}} rice, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer. Cover loosely and cook about 18 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the rice is tender.
Taste, adjust salt, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Rice will thicken the soup; add broth or water when reheating.

title: Sheet-Pan Sausage & Potatoes
description: Roasted sausage and potatoes with very little hands-on work.
substitutions: Add chunks of cabbage or bell pepper for the last 20 minutes.

steps.text: Add sausage and roast 18–20 minutes more.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a sheet pan if you want easier cleanup.
Toss {{potatoes}} halved baby potatoes with {{oil}} oil, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Spread the potatoes cut-side down and roast for 15 minutes.
Add {{sausage}} sliced smoked sausage to the pan and stir everything once.
Roast another 18–20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and browned.
Serve straight from the pan.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in oven, air fryer, or skillet for best texture.

title: Creamy White Beans on Toast
description: Creamy savory white beans spooned over toast for a fast pantry meal.
substitutions: A squeeze of lemon brightens it up.

steps.text: Warm beans with butter, seasoning, and broth.

cookSteps.text: Warm {{butter}} butter or oil in a small skillet.
Add {{beans}} drained white beans, garlic powder, black pepper, and {{broth}} broth or water.
Simmer 5–6 minutes. Mash some of the beans with the back of a spoon so the liquid turns creamy.
Toast {{bread}} bread.
Spoon the creamy beans over the toast. Add parmesan if using and serve.

storage: Refrigerate leftover beans up to 4 days; toast fresh bread when serving.

title: Egg & Cheese Breakfast Wrap
description: Soft scrambled eggs and cheese in a warm tortilla; fast enough for a workday.
substitutions: Add leftover vegetables or a small amount of diced ham.

steps.text: Add cheese and eggs, then roll.

cookSteps.text: Beat {{eggs}} eggs with a fork.
Melt {{butter}} butter in a small skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the eggs and gently stir until softly set, about 2–3 minutes.
Warm {{tortilla}} tortilla for a few seconds so it bends easily.
Put {{cheese}} shredded cheese and the eggs in the center. Add salsa if using, fold the sides in, and roll it up.

storage: Best fresh. Cooked eggs can be refrigerated up to 3 days.
